physics.energy-resources-extended-kb.001.a: wind; solar (also hydro, tidal, geothermal, biomass)
physics.energy-resources-extended-kb.001.b: Coal: reliable/constant output, controllable to demand, cheaper/existing tech; but non-renewable, CO2 (global warming), SO2 (acid rain). Wind: renewable, no CO2 when running, free fuel; but unreliable (wind varies), many turbines/large area, visual/noise, high initial cost. Judgement: wind better long-term with backup.

physics.energy-resources-recall-kb.0007.a: a resource that will not run out / is replenished as used
physics.energy-resources-recall-kb.0007.b: releases CO2 causing global warming (or SO2 acid rain; non-renewable)

physics.energy-thermal-describe-kb.0010.a: air near heater heated, expands, less dense, rises; cooler denser air sinks to replace it; circulation
physics.energy-thermal-describe-kb.0010.b: land heats faster than sea; air above land warms, less dense, rises; cooler air from over sea moves in to replace it (breeze from sea to land)
physics.energy-thermal-describe-kb.0010.c: Leslie cube with hot water, dull black and shiny faces; IR detector/thermometer at same distance from each face; black face gives higher reading

physics.energy-thermal-explain-kb.0002.all: white surfaces are poor absorbers / good reflectors of infrared radiation, so the house absorbs less heat and stays cooler

physics.energy-thermal-extended-kb.0013.b: loft insulation and cavity wall insulation trap air (poor conductor) and stop convection; double glazing - gap of air/vacuum reduces conduction; draught excluders reduce convection; reflective foil behind radiators/shiny surfaces reduce radiation loss; carpets reduce conduction

physics.energy-thermal-recall-kb.0005.b: they have free (delocalised) electrons that transfer energy

physics.energy-transfers-describe-kb.001.a: electrical energy -> thermal energy store of water (some wasted heating kettle/surroundings, sound)
physics.energy-transfers-describe-kb.001.b: the energy transfers in a device: input, useful and wasted energy; width of arrows proportional to amount

physics.energy-transfers-recall-kb.0002.all: any two of: mechanically (force/work), electrically, by heating, by radiation (light/sound)

physics.energy-work-explain-kb.0013.a: some energy transferred to thermal (and sound) on impact/air resistance, so less KE converted back to GPE
physics.energy-work-explain-kb.0013.b: same work done (same weight, same height) but in less time; power = work/time
physics.energy-work-explain-kb.0013.c: KE = 1/2 mv^2 so doubling speed quadruples KE; brakes must do 4x work; braking force same so braking distance x4

physics.energy-work-recall-kb.0010.a: work done = force x distance moved
physics.energy-work-recall-kb.0010.b: GPE = m x g x h

physics.fo-force-diagram.0012.a: forward driving force and backward drag/friction, equal lengths; weight down and normal reaction up, equal

physics.fo-stopping.0004.c: stopping distance increases because reaction time increases so thinking distance increases

physics.forces-elasticity-explain-kb.000.a: extension not proportional to force; force-extension graph not a straight line
physics.forces-elasticity-explain-kb.000.b: spring may continue to extend / oscillate; wait for it to come to rest so reading is accurate

physics.forces-elasticity-mcq-kb.0004.all: the initial straight-line section through the origin

physics.forces-elasticity-recall-kb.0004.a: extension is directly proportional to force applied (up to limit of proportionality)

physics.forces-forces-describe-kb.0001.all: at start only weight acts (air resistance zero), accelerates; as speed increases air resistance increases, resultant force decreases, acceleration decreases; at terminal velocity air resistance = weight, resultant zero

physics.forces-forces-explain-kb.0002.all: parachute increases surface area so air resistance increases greatly; air resistance > weight so resultant force upwards; decelerates until air resistance = weight again (new lower terminal velocity)

physics.forces-forces-extended-kb.0005.a: same direction: add; opposite directions: subtract (larger minus smaller), direction of larger
physics.forces-forces-extended-kb.0005.b: stopping = thinking + braking. Thinking: speed, reaction time (tiredness, alcohol, drugs, distractions). Braking: speed, mass, condition of brakes/tyres, road surface (wet/icy). Speed affects both; braking distance increases more (KE ~ v^2)

physics.forces-forces-recall-kb.0011.b: wet/icy road, worn tyres/brakes, higher speed, greater mass

physics.forces-moments-explain-kb.0013.a: the force on the support nearer the person increases; at left end left support takes most; as person walks right, left support force decreases and right increases; total equals weight of plank+person (moments about a support)
physics.forces-moments-explain-kb.0013.b: balance the rule on a knife edge/pivot, move until it balances horizontally; the balance point is the centre of gravity (should be at 50 cm)

physics.forces-moments-mcq-kb.0009.b: the sum of clockwise moments equals the sum of anticlockwise moments

physics.forces-moments-recall-kb.0011.a: moment = force x perpendicular distance from pivot
physics.forces-moments-recall-kb.0011.b: increase the force; increase the perpendicular distance from pivot

physics.forces-momentum-explain-kb.0002.all: momentum before firing is zero; momentum conserved; bullet gains momentum forward so gun gains equal momentum backwards, gun moves backward (smaller velocity as larger mass)
